claims.text: An aluminum-based alloy containing selected additions such as Li, Mg, or Sc will have significantly lower density than conventional aluminum alloys.
The modified aluminum alloy will maintain or improve mechanical strength relative to conventional aluminum alloys.
The modified aluminum alloy will maintain or improve durability relative to conventional aluminum alloys.
The modified aluminum alloy will maintain or improve processability relative to conventional aluminum alloys.
The selected alloying elements will refine the aluminum-alloy microstructure.
Solid-solution strengthening will contribute to the proposed microstructural refinement and strengthening.
Precipitation hardening will contribute to the proposed microstructural refinement and strengthening.
The modification will produce well-distributed strengthening precipitates.
The modification will produce a homogeneous solid solution.
The refined microstructure will enhance load transfer.
The alloying additions will lower the intrinsic density of the aluminum matrix.
The alloying additions will promote formation of fine strengthening precipitates.
The strengthening mechanism will maintain ductility.
The modified alloy will exhibit increased yield strength relative to the unmodified baseline.
The modified alloy will exhibit increased hardness relative to the unmodified baseline.
The combined density and mechanical-property changes will improve the alloy's weight-performance ratio.
The proposed improvements are expected under ambient or moderate structural-service conditions.
Extreme-temperature, corrosive, or specialized environments may require additional alloy modifications.
